--- Slide/Halaman 3 ---
OESOPHAGUS
• Pars Cervicalis
– Panjang 5-6 cm, v. cervicalis VI s.d. v. 
thoracalis I
– Anterior melekat dengan trachea
– Anterolateral tertutup oleh kelenjar tiroid
– Sisi dextra/sinistra dipersarafi oleh nervus
recurren laryngeus
– Posterior berbatasan dengan hipofaring
– Pada bagian lateral ada carotid sheath beserta
isinya


--- Slide/Halaman 4 ---
OESOPHAGUS
• Pars Thoracalis
– Panjang 16-18 cm, v. thoracalis II-IX
– Berada di mediastinum superior antara trakea dan
kolumna vertebralis
– Dalam rongga toraks disilang oleh arcus aorta setinggi
v. thoracalis IV dan bronkus utama sinistra setinggi v. 
thoracalis V
– Arteri pulmonalis dextra menyilang di bawah bifurcatio
trachealis
– Pada bagian distal antara dinding posterior esofagus
dan ventralcorpus vertebralis terdapat ductus
thoracicus, vena azygos, arteri dan vena intercostalis


--- Slide/Halaman 5 ---
OESOPHAGUS
• Pars Abdominalis
–Terdapat pars diaphragmatica
sepanjang 1 - 1,5 cm, setinggi v. 
thoracalis X s.d. v. lumbalis III
–Terdapat pars abdominalis sepanjang
2 - 3 cm, bergabung dengan cardia
gaster disebut gastroesophageal
junction

OESOPHAGUS

VASKULARISASI OESOPHAGUS
Esofagus bagian thorak :
• Arteri dari cabang aorta thoracalis dan
arteri thyroid inferior (cabang dari trunchus
thyrocervicalis) 
• Vena dari cabang vena azygous dan vena 
thyroid inferior


--- Slide/Halaman 9 ---
VASKULARISASI OESOPHAGUS
Esofagus bagian abdomen :
• Arteri gastrica sinistra (cabang dari trunchus
coeliaca) dan arteri phrenicus inferior 
• Vena berasal dari 2 rute :
– Sirkulasi portal melalui vena gastrika
– Sirkulasi sistemik melalui vena azygous
– Kedua rute membentuk porto-systemic 
anastomosis (hubungan antara sistem portal 
dan sistemik)

SISTEM LIMFATIK OESOPHAGUS
• Terbagi 3 :
–Superior third – deep cervical lymph 
nodes.
–Middle third – superior and 
posterior mediastinal nodes.
–Lower third – left gastric and celiac 
nodes.

The large intestine comes after the small

LARGE INTESTINE


--- Slide/Halaman 45 ---
➢
➢cecum
cecum
➔is the proximal end of the large intestine and is where 
the large and small intestines meet at the ileocecel 
junction. 
➔it is located in the right lower quadrantof the abdomen 
near the iliac fossa.
➔is a sac that extends inferiorly about 6cm past the 
ileocecal junction.
➔Appendix is attached to the cecum is a tube about 9 
cm long.


--- Slide/Halaman 46 ---


--- Slide/Halaman 47 ---
➢
➢colon
colon
➔is the last part of the digestive system in most 
vertebrates. It extracts water and salt from solid wastes
before they are eliminated from the body and is the site 
in which flora-aided (large bacterial) fermentation of 
unabsorbed material occurs. Unlike the small intestine, 
the colon does not play a major role in absorption of 
foods and nutrients. However, the colon does absorb 
water, sodium and some fat soluble vitamins.


--- Slide/Halaman 48 ---


--- Slide/Halaman 49 ---
- is a straight , muscular tube that begins at the termination of the sigmoid 
colon and ends at the anal canal. The muscular tunic is smooth muscle and 
it is relatively thick in the rectum compared with the rest of the digestive 
tract.
- is continuous above with the sigmoid colon, while below it ends in anal 
canal. From its origin at the level of the third sacral vertebral its passes 
downward, lying in the sacrococcygeal curve and extends for about 2.5 cm 
in front of  and a little below, the tip of the coccyx as far as the apex of the 
prostate. 
➢
➢Rectum
Rectum


--- Slide/Halaman 50 ---


--- Slide/Halaman 51 ---
Anal Canal
Anal Canal
- the last 2-3 cm of the digestive tract. It can begins at the inferior end of the 
rectum and ends at the anus. 
- the smooth  muscle of the anal canal is even thicker than that of the 
rectum and forms the internal anal sphincter at the superior end of the anal 
canal. The external anal sphincter at the inferior end of the anal canal is 
formed by skeletal muscle. 


--- Slide/Halaman 52 ---


--- Slide/Halaman 53 ---
Lymphatic drainage
•The ascending colon and proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon
is to the colic lymph nodes and the superior mesenteric lymph nodes
•The distal one-third of the transverse colon, the descending colon, 
the sigmoid colon, and the upper rectum drain into the inferior 
mesenteric and colic lymph nodes
•The lower rectum to the anal canal drain to the internal iliac nodes
•The anal canal drains into the superficial inguinal nodes
Blood supply
Arterial : superior mesenteric artery
and inferior mesenteric artery
Venous : inferior mesenteric vein draining into the splenic vein, and 
superior mesenteric vein joining the splenic vein to form the 
hepatic portal vein
